title: How can Ruhee tell how much longer one screw is?
description: Ruhee sees a toy mended with a second screw that looks just like the first, and then spots that one screw is a little longer. A ruler with only big marks is held under them, and the video stops on a question about the tiny gap.
teaching_notes: One idea: a whole mark of a ruler cannot name a very small gap. Ask each child to say how they would measure it, and do not confirm any guess. Watch for students who say the screws are equal because both fall on the same mark.

source: Two screws that look the same
video_script.why: Before any smaller unit is named, the child meets two real screws whose small difference a whole mark cannot show.
video_script.substitution: Picture two screws side by side over a ruler that has only the big marks, and a gap too small to name.
video_script.anchor: Two screws that look the same, with one a little longer than the other

names.Ruhee: the child who watches the mother mend a toy with a screw

never_show: the word tenth or the decimal point
any way of measuring the gap
maths_rules: The two screws differ by a small amount in length, and no length is shown or said.
The ruler in the hook has only the big marks.
The open question: how can the small gap be measured. No unit and no length is shown or hinted.
video_script.design: One idea: a whole mark cannot name a very small gap. Assumes the child has used a ruler. No wrong idea is broken. The photo sits as a dimmed backdrop in the first beat and fades at its end; the drawn screws arrive after it and stay to the end.
